concepts.name: What GPS is
concepts.source_span: GPS stands for Global Positioning System.

questions.stem: What does GPS stand for?
Which country built and runs GPS?
Does a GPS receiver send signals to the satellites?
How does a phone work out where it is with GPS?
options: By listening to radio signals from satellites

questions.stem: Why can any number of phones use GPS at the same time?
options: Each phone has its own satellite
The satellites broadcast and receivers only listen, so phones add no load
Only a few phones can use it at once

questions.stem: What does a phone need from each satellite to work out its position?
options: A reply to a message the phone sent
The satellite's position and the exact time its signal was sent

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT needed for GPS to find your position?
options: The time each signal was sent

concepts.name: The satellites
concepts.source_span: The satellites orbit about 20,200 kilometres above the Earth.

questions.stem: At about what height do GPS satellites orbit?
How many orbital planes does the GPS constellation have?
About how often does a GPS satellite circle the Earth?
What do GPS satellites carry for accurate timing?
About how many times does a GPS satellite circle the Earth in one week?
Why does each satellite carry very accurate atomic clocks?
options: Positions depend on knowing exactly when each signal was sent

questions.stem: Spread evenly, at least how many satellites are in each of the six orbital planes?

concepts.name: Measuring distance with time
concepts.source_span: Distance equals the speed of light multiplied by the travel time.

questions.stem: How is the distance to a satellite calculated?
options: Speed of light multiplied by the travel time
Height of the satellite divided by 2
Time divided by the speed of light
Speed of sound divided by time

questions.stem: At what speed do radio signals travel?
options: The speed of the satellite only

questions.stem: About how long does a GPS signal take to reach the ground?
What does the receiver compare to find the travel time?
options: The arrival time and the time the signal was sent

questions.stem: A signal takes about 0.07 seconds to arrive. About how far has it travelled?
If a signal took twice as long to arrive, how far away would the satellite be?
Why must the receiver know exactly when each signal was sent?
options: Distance comes from travel time, so it needs both the sending and arrival times

concepts.name: Trilateration
concepts.source_span: Trilateration finds a position from its distances to several known points.

questions.stem: What does trilateration find?
options: A position from distances to several known points

questions.stem: The distance to one satellite places the receiver on:
options: A straight line to the Earth

questions.stem: Two satellites narrow the position down to:
options: A circle where two spheres meet

questions.stem: Three satellites narrow the position down to:
options: A single point on the ground every time
Two points, one usually far out in space

questions.stem: How does the receiver get its distance to each satellite?
Which list is right, satellite by satellite?
options: One: a circle; two: a sphere; three: one point
One: a sphere; two: a circle; three: two points
One: a point; two: a line; three: a sphere
One: two points; two: a circle; three: a sphere

questions.stem: What does each extra satellite distance do to the possible position?

concepts.name: Why four satellites are needed
concepts.source_span: A fourth satellite lets the receiver solve for its own clock error as well as its three position coordinates.

questions.stem: Why is a fourth satellite needed?
options: To solve for the receiver's own clock error

questions.stem: Why is the receiver's clock a problem?
options: It is cheaper and less accurate than an atomic clock
It is too fast to read

questions.stem: What does a small clock error turn into?
How many satellite signals does a receiver need at least?
A receiver's clock is 1 millisecond fast. About how wrong would its distances be if nothing corrected it?
Why can phones use a cheap clock instead of an atomic one?
options: Phones get atomic time from the mobile network
Cheap clocks are just as accurate
The fourth satellite's signal lets the receiver work out its own clock error
The satellites correct each phone's clock directly

questions.stem: Which order is right?
options: Satellite sends its position and time, receiver notes the arrival time, works out distances, then solves for position and clock error
Receiver works out distances, satellite sends time, receiver notes arrival, then solves
Receiver solves for position, notes arrival time, satellite sends time, then works out distances
Satellite sends time, receiver solves for position, notes arrival, then works out distances

concepts.name: Relativity and corrections
concepts.source_span: The net effect of their speed and weaker gravity is that the satellite clocks run faster by about 38 microseconds per day compared with clocks on the ground.

questions.stem: Which theory affects the satellite clocks?
By about how much do the satellite clocks run faster each day?
What would happen to GPS positions without the correction?
options: They would drift by several kilometres each day
They would be wrong only at night

questions.stem: How is the relativity effect handled?
options: The satellite clocks are adjusted so the correction is built in

questions.stem: Without any correction, about how much time would a satellite clock gain on ground clocks over 10 days?
Why does a clock error of only 38 microseconds a day matter for GPS?
options: Light travels so far in that time that positions would be off by kilometres

questions.stem: If the relativity correction were switched off, about how far off would positions be after one week?

concepts.name: Other systems and accuracy
concepts.source_span: Other global systems are GLONASS from Russia, Galileo from the European Union and BeiDou from China.

questions.stem: Which system is Russia's global navigation system?
Which system belongs to the European Union?
Which system belongs to China?
What is NavIC?
Between tall office buildings your map shows you 40 metres from where you really are. What is the likely reason?
options: The buildings block or reflect the satellite signals
The satellites are switched off in cities
Too many people are using GPS

questions.stem: Counting GPS, how many global navigation systems do the notes name?
Where is a phone's GPS likely to be most accurate?
options: In an open field under a clear sky
